answers.answer:
Summary: In SCOPe 2.04 the ColG collagen-binding domain (PDB 1nqd, d1nqda_, sunid 86025) and the Cry3A C-terminal domain (PDB 1dlc, d1dlca1, sunid 23719) shared only the all-beta class. In current SCOPe 2.08 they share the Galactose-binding domain-like superfamily (b.18.1), which is SCOPe's positive assertion of probable common ancestry, while remaining in different families. The change is a reclassification of the ColG domain, not of the Cry3A domain.

Verified SCOPe facts (retrieved, release-scoped):
- SCOPe 2.04: d1nqda_ = b.23.2.1, lineage class b (All beta proteins) > fold b.23 'CUB-like' (sunid 49853; 'sandwich, 10 strands in 2 sheets; jelly-roll') > superfamily b.23.2 'Collagen-binding domain' (sunid 89260; comment 'N-terminal strand appears only in calcium-free form') > family b.23.2.1 'Collagen-binding domain' (sunid 89261) > protein 'Class 1 collagenase' > species Clostridium histolyticum. d1dlca1 (1dlc A:500-644) = b.18.1.3, lineage b > fold b.18 'Galactose-binding domain-like' (sunid 49784) > superfamily b.18.1 (sunid 49785) > family b.18.1.3 'delta-Endotoxin, C-terminal domain' (sunid 49796) > species Bacillus thuringiensis tenebrionis CRYIIIA. compare_scop_domains in 2.04 reports relationship 'same_class', lowest shared node sunid 48724 (class b). Different folds, so SCOPe 2.04 made no homology assertion and did not even assert fold-level similarity.
- SCOPe 2.08 (current stable; freeze 2021-07-28): d1nqda_ = b.18.1.36, lineage b > b.18 (sunid 49784; 'sandwich; 9 strands in 2 sheets; jelly-roll') > b.18.1 (sunid 49785) > new family b.18.1.36 'Collagen-binding domain' (sunid 267607) > 'Class 1 collagenase' (sunid 267633) > C. histolyticum (sunid 267693). The 1nqd B chain was also re-split into d1nqdb1 (B:893-1008, b.18.1.36) plus a tiny l.1.1.1 segment d1nqdb2 (B:891-892). d1dlca1 is unchanged at b.18.1.3 (sunids 23719/49796 identical in both releases). compare_scop_domains in 2.08 reports 'same_superfamily', lowest shared node b.18.1 (sunid 49785). The old superfamily identifier b.23.2 returns 404 in 2.08, consistent with the superfamily being retired when its only family was moved under b.18.1. No homology warnings, heterogeneity, or inconsistency flags exist on either domain, either family, or the b.18.1 superfamily in 2.08.
- Curated rationale recorded in SCOPe: the family b.18.1.36 annotation states 'PubMed 17977833 describes likely homology between d2quoa_, d1w99a3, and d1nqdb_'. d2quoa_ is the Clostridium perfringens enterotoxin (CPE) C-terminal domain, family b.18.1.37; d1w99a3 is the Cry4Ba delta-endotoxin C-terminal domain, family b.18.1.3, i.e. the same family as the Cry3A domain d1dlca1; d1nqdb_ is the ColG collagen-binding domain. So the SCOPe curators moved ColG CBD into b.18.1 on the basis of that publication's structure-based homology argument linking the collagenase CBD, CPE C-terminal domain, and Cry delta-endotoxin domain III. The delta-endotoxin family b.18.1.3 is additionally mapped to Pfam PF03944.

Structural evidence in SCOPe's stored comparisons: 1nqdA itself has no stored hits; its 90%-identity cluster representative is 1nqjA (99.2% identity over 119 of 122 residues), so the following are representative evidence, not direct 1nqd results. FATCAT structure hits for 1nqjA (filters: P<0.05, initial RMSD<4 Å, page of 50 with more available) include: d5ikua1 (b.18.1.36, second ColG CBD, P=4.2e-14, RMSD 1.72 Å, 28.7% identity), d2quoa_ (b.18.1.37 CPE C-terminal domain, P=1.4e-6, score 151.6, RMSD 2.49 Å, 10.3% identity, 96 chain residues aligned), d2xh6a2 (b.18.1.0 automated match to the same CPE domain, P=1.9e-6), d1wmfa1 (b.18.1.20, P=2.0e-6), and d1w99a3 (b.18.1.3 Cry4Ba domain III, P=3.95e-3, score 94.2, RMSD 2.52 Å, 2.5% identity, 94 chain residues aligned). BLAST sequence hits for 1nqjA reach only other collagenase CBDs and b.18.1.0 automated matches (best non-self log10 E = -16.9 to d5sv5a_, b.18.1.0); no delta-endotoxin domain is a sequence hit, so the relationship is below sequence detection and is structure-discovered. The FATCAT list also contains competing non-b.18 superfamilies at weaker P-values (e.g. b.14.1 calpain domain III P=1.8e-6 with RMSD 1.39 Å; b.132.1, b.179.1, b.23.1 CUB at P=1.3e-3, b.23.4). Fold-level jelly-roll similarity therefore does not by itself discriminate b.18.1 from other beta-sandwich superfamilies; the superfamily-level call rests on the curated literature-based judgment plus the consistent b.18.1 top hits.

Functional evidence consistent with common ancestry (interpretation, not a SCOPe assertion): the b.18.1 superfamily is named for galactose-binding (carbohydrate-binding) jelly-roll domains, and both domains discussed here are non-catalytic C-terminal binding modules: ColG CBD binds collagen (PDB keywords: 'collagen-binding domain, calcium'; SCOPe 2.04 superfamily note that the N-terminal strand is seen only in the calcium-free form, i.e. calcium-dependent conformational behaviour), and Cry delta-endotoxin domain III is the receptor/carbohydrate-recognition domain of the toxin.
